The core challenge is representing a set of calibrated forecasts as a convex combination of extreme points. The authors map this to a polyhedral geometry problem: the set of feasible output experts forms a convex cone K within the row space of the observable signal matrix A. Decomposing the all-ones vector into nonnegative generators of K yields valid refined experts. This duality between forecast calibration and polyhedral combinatorics provides a computationally tractable framework for optimal aggregation.
